sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Grayson County
sections.html:
Deeds for Grayson County land are recorded at the Grayson County Clerk's office, 125 East Market Street, Leitchfield, KY 42754. KRS 382.110 sends a deed to the clerk of whichever county contains the land, or most of it. Recording is what makes the deed stand up against later buyers and creditors who never saw it.

Two numbers matter for property work. Recording and delinquent taxes are at (270) 259-5295. The licensing and transfers desk is at (270) 259-3201. The office keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:00 and opens the second Saturday of each month from 8:00 to 11:00. If your closing is set for a specific day, call ahead and confirm the office will be open.

Land in Leitchfield, Caneyville, Clarkson, Big Clifty or out near the lakes is all filed in this one office. The Clerk's website has an online records section where you can look up older instruments, which helps when you need the deed that put the current owner on title.

sections.h2: Kentucky transfer tax on a sale
sections.html:
Kentucky charges fifty cents on every $500 of price, rounding a leftover partial block up. Responsibility falls on the seller. When the deed is handed in, the Clerk does the math. Nothing gets recorded until the Clerk has the money, so bring it to closing.

For a gift, or a deed that recites only nominal money, the value used is what the property would bring on the open market. Liens on the property count toward the value of a sale. One transaction is taxed once. Of what the Clerk collects, 5 percent covers the office's handling and the remainder goes to the county treasurer's general fund.

Ask the Clerk's recording desk for the exact figure before closing day so the seller's net sheet is right and the title company has a number to put on the settlement statement.

The statute exempts many transfers. Ordinary homeowners tend to run into these:

  • a deed that only pledges property for a debt, or lifts that pledge;
  • a correction deed, or a confirmation of one already of record;
  • a deed from one spouse to the other, including ex-spouses dividing property in a divorce;
  • a foreclosure, or an owner handing the house back to the lender to avoid one;
  • a sale for unpaid taxes or assessments, and a partition among co-owners;
  • a token-price deed from a parent to a child or a grandparent to a grandchild.

A transfer into a trust is also free of the tax when the grantor is the only beneficiary. A clerk who willfully records a taxable deed without collecting can be fined $50 per offense, so expect the Clerk's staff to look closely at the price or value stated on your deed.

sections.h2: Tracing the owner's title in the deed
sections.html:
Each deed must point back to how the seller came to own the land. If an earlier deed was recorded, the new deed cites its office, book, page and recording date. If the land came by inheritance or another unrecorded route, the deed explains how and from whom the grantor took title.

If the parcel was pieced together from several sources, the deed names each one and marks the portion that came from each. Clerks are barred from accepting a deed that omits the trail. Deeds from court commissioners, sheriffs and other court officers acting in that role are outside the rule.

When a house has stayed in one family, the earlier deed may be decades old, and the book and page reference is the only link a title examiner can follow back. Before anyone drafts the new deed, pull the last deed that vested title in the current owner. A wrong book and page cite sends the paper back to whoever prepared it, which can delay a closing.

sections.h2: Deadlines for a deed in lieu or a commissioner's deed
sections.html:
Recording deadlines for lender and court deeds
Type of deedWho must fileDeadline
Deed in lieu of foreclosureThe lenderWithin 45 days of the signing date
Commissioner's deed after a judicial saleThe granteeWithin five business days of receiving it
Commissioner's deed still unfiledA city whose limits include the property may petition Circuit CourtAfter 30 business days without a filing

In a petition the court can order the deed filed and add court costs and attorney fees. For an owner in default, these dates decide how long the borrower's name stays on the record. Until the lender's deed is filed, the public index still shows the borrower as the owner.

sections.h2: Unpaid property tax and the Clerk
sections.html:
An unpaid bill leaves the sheriff at closing time on April 15 and goes to the Clerk, who records a lien. Each month, or part of one, adds one percent interest, and both the Clerk and the county attorney charge a commission on top. A sale of the tax certificate can be scheduled from day 90 to day 135 after the transfer, and an outside buyer at that sale adds costs of their own.

Because the lien attaches to the parcel, any title search the buyer orders will turn it up. If you are selling, call the Clerk's delinquent tax line at (270) 259-5295 and ask for an exact payoff before the closing date. Usually the payoff comes out of the seller's proceeds at the closing table.

sections.h2: What to bring when you record
sections.html:
Treat the Clerk's counter as the last stop before the sale is public record. The title company or attorney usually carries the paperwork over, but a seller handling things directly should have the signed deed, the money for the transfer tax and the recording fee, and a copy of the earlier deed showing how the grantor got title. If a mortgage is being paid off, the release should be on its way to the same office.

Here is how a typical closing flows. Back taxes get paid off, the deed is signed, the Clerk works out the transfer tax, and the deed is then recorded and indexed. Once it is indexed, the buyer's name replaces yours in the public record.

A quick cash sale avoids a lender's conditions, yet the filing steps do not change. The deed still has to cite the prior title, and the tax still has to be paid before the Clerk accepts it.

Population in 2025 was 27,406, a 3.7 percent rise over 2020. Of its 13,496 housing units, 74.6 percent are owner-occupied. Median home value is $164,600 and median gross rent is $658. With just 36 building permits in 2025, new construction is a small slice of the market. Resales of older houses dominate, and an owner facing deferred repairs may prefer a cash buyer willing to take the place as is.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Grayson County Clerk?
faqs.a: 125 East Market Street, Leitchfield, KY 42754. For recording and delinquent tax questions call (270) 259-5295. Weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:00.

faqs.q: Who owes the transfer tax on a Grayson County house sale?
faqs.a: The seller. The rate is fifty cents per $500 of value, and the Clerk collects it before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does a deed in lieu of foreclosure carry the transfer tax?
faqs.a: No, KRS 142.050 excuses that transfer. The lender must still record the deed within 45 days of signing it.

faqs.q: What if my deed leaves out how I got title?
faqs.a: The Clerk cannot accept it. The deed must cite the earlier recorded deed by book and page, or explain how title arrived by inheritance or other unrecorded means.

faqs.q: Do old property taxes get paid when a Grayson County house sells?
faqs.a: Yes, normally at closing, since the lien stays on the parcel. Get a payoff quote from the Clerk's delinquent tax line first.
